verdict.interpretation: On SIFT-1M (their dataset) with their N_k/in-degree framework: anti-hub-target (outlier) queries need more distance computations than typical queries at the same budget -- reproducing their Theorem-2 latency/NDC instability -- while overall recall stays high and max in-degree sits in our safe regime (<200), exactly as our in-degree law predicts for clean data. Injecting a duplicate sink pushes max in-degree ~1000x into our collapse regime where recall craters: this is their Theorem-1 Hub Capture taken to the extreme. One N_k axis, two regimes, two metrics (their latency tail at the low-in-degree/anti-hub end; our silent recall collapse at the extreme high-in-degree/duplicate-hub end).
